title: Hyundai, Nvidia and LG Form AI Self-Driving Alliance to Take On Tesla
source_used: Seoul Economic Daily (English edition, AI-translated from Korean; original reporting by Koo Kyung-woo)
key_facts: Industry sources say (5 Oct 2026) that LG and Nvidia have launched a project to commercialise a next-generation 'AI DV' platform, after LG Chairman Koo Kwang-mo and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang met in August and signed a memorandum of understanding on strategic business cooperation.

AI DV goes a step beyond the software-defined vehicle: AI, rather than ordinary software, drives overall vehicle operation, using large language and vision language models to recognise and predict surroundings in real time. The article does not spell out what 'DV' stands for.
The two companies have begun developing a high-performance computing platform that combines Nvidia's Drive Hyperion autonomous-driving system with LG's in-vehicle infotainment and software.

The partnership is expected to bear fruit in Hyundai Motor Group's first mass-produced autonomous vehicle; Hyundai said earlier it would start mass-producing Level 2++ vehicles with Nvidia technology in 2028; Hyundai is 'said to be reviewing' ways to use LG infotainment.
The paper describes an 'AI DV triangle': Hyundai Motor Group supplies vehicles and driving data, Nvidia the AI computing and driving 'brain', LG the in-car digital experience.
LG Electronics already supplies infotainment to Genesis (G90, GV80, G80) and Kia (Carnival, EV3).
The paper expects an autonomous vehicle from this combination to shake up a market led by Tesla, which rolled out FSD (Supervised) v14 Lite in South Korea in July.
quote_evidence: According to industry sources on Oct. 5, LG and Nvidia have launched a project to commercialize a next-generation AI DV platform.
Hyundai is said to be reviewing various ways to use LG infotainment as it develops mass-production models based on Nvidia's autonomous-driving system.
An autonomous vehicle built by the Hyundai Motor Group-Nvidia-LG combination is expected to shake up a market led by Tesla.
why_it_matters_hint: If it goes ahead, Hyundai and Kia cars could get more advanced AI-based driving help from 2028 (Hyundai's stated Level 2++ plan with Nvidia), in a market where Tesla launched its supervised self-driving software in Korea in July.
event_date: Reported 5 Oct 2026; the LG and Nvidia memorandum was signed in August 2026; Hyundai's Level 2++ mass production is planned for 2028.
notes: Read in full. The paper's headline says an alliance is formed, but the text reports only an LG and Nvidia project (unnamed industry sources) with Hyundai's role expected or under review, so the headline overstates and the score is lowered by 1. Level 2++ is an industry label for advanced driver assistance that is short of driverless.
